abstract: N,N-dimethylacetamide, hexamethylene bisacetamide, and Polybrene induced rapid and extensive differentiation in vitro in an otherwise slowly differentiating subline of embryonal carcinoma cells. The type of differentiated cell induced was dependent on the spatial organization of the stem cells during drug treatment. In monalayer culture "epithelial" cells were produced exclusively. However, treatment of aggregated suspension cultures yielded predominantly "fibroblast-like" cells. The undifferentiated embryonal carcinoma cells and the two differentiated cell types were morphologically distinct when examined by light microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and transmission electron microscopy; and they had differences in cell surface antigens. Both differential cell types produced large amounts of fibronectin, whereas the embryonal carcinoma cells produced only minimal amounts. This system provides a convenient way to induce relatively synchronous differentiation of embryonal carcinoma cells into specific differentiated cell types.
abstract_ja: N,N-ジメチルアセトアミド、ヘキサメチレンビスアセトアミド、ポリブレンは、分化が緩徐な胎児性癌細胞の亜株において、in vitroで急速かつ広範な分化を誘導した。誘導される分化細胞の種類は、薬剤処理中の幹細胞の空間的配置に依存した。単層培養では「上皮様」細胞のみが産生されたが、凝集浮遊培養を処理すると主に「線維芽細胞様」細胞が得られた。未分化の胎児性癌細胞と2種類の分化細胞は、光学顕微鏡、走査型電子顕微鏡、透過型電子顕微鏡で形態学的に区別でき、細胞表面抗原にも違いがあった。両分化細胞ともフィブロネクチンを多量に産生したが、胎児性癌細胞はごくわずかしか産生しなかった。本系は、胎児性癌細胞を比較的同期した形で特定の分化細胞へ誘導する簡便な方法を提供する。
